newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans to keep watch on paedophiles.
newsitem.headline: France plans to keep watch on paedophiles.

text.p: France's government said on Tuesday it wanted to keep repeat child sex offenders under medical surveillance once they were freed from jail, as part of a crackdown on paedophiles.
"In a few weeks we will have prepared...a draft bill designed to better punish sexual abuse and attacks," Justice Minister Jacques Toubon told the National Assembly.
Toubon said the bill, worked out after shock over the sex abuse and murder of four children in neighbouring Belgium, would especially seek to sanction paedophiles who abused children more than once.

"We will introduce a new punishment for these criminals into our penal code...of a mandatory medical surveillance," Toubon said in reply to a question. Repeat offenders would undergo court-ordered medical tests after they had served jail terms.

Toubon also said the centre-right government wanted to expand medical and psychological treatment for paedophiles while they were in jail at 24 centres around France. The draft law would probably be ready for debate by parliament in early 1997.
The crackdown would also make it easier to seize pornography featuring children or adolescents and punish anyone caught with it, Toubon said.
France aimed to tighten coordination within the government to combat paedophilia, giving Education Minister Francois Bayrou overall responsibility.
Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe would formally announce the plan for cracking down on paedophiles on November 20, Toubon said.
